newsitem.title: USA: Daimler-Benz plans convertible note offer.
newsitem.headline: Daimler-Benz plans convertible note offer.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aktiengesellschaft said on Wednesday it planned to offer about DM 1.0 billion aggregate principal amount of 5 3/4 percent subordinated mandatory convertible notes due June 14, 2002.

The offering, which was subject to the effectiveness of a registration statement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, would be made through a rights offering to all holders of record of American Depositary Shares (ADS) as of April 25, 1995.
The company said it expected rights would be made available to holders on or about April 28, 1997 and could be exercised until May 13, 1997.
Application has been made to list the rights for trading on the New York Stock Exchange, it said. Daimler said it expected the offer to close on or about May 15, 1997.

Each outstanding share or ADS would entitle the holder to one right, the company said. An estimated 67 rights would entitle the holder to subscribe for one note, it said, adding the exact subscription ratio would be determined on April 18.

Notes would be convertible at the option of the holder into shares at a conversion premium of between 11 percent and 16 percent above the average market price of the shares during the period between April 28 and May 6, 1997, Daimler said.

At maturity, notes would be mandatorily converted into shares at a rate determined based on the price performance of shares during a 20 trading day period prior to June 8, 2002, subject to a minimum and maximum conversion price, it said.
